messages:
maria: FYI a customer hit a nasty onboarding crash on workers. They import our package normally and the runtime throws 'TypeError: Redwood is not a function'.
jamal: Which bundler/runtime? any repro?
maria: Cloudflare Workers via Wrangler + rollup. Their bundler picked our CJS entry even though they're in an ESM worker. Root issue looks like our package exports map points at the CJS file.
lia: Oof. If exports resolves to CJS, ESM runtimes will get a module shape mismatch. Also saw TypeScript in their build complain that types were using `export =` which confuses modern TS config.
jamal: That can also explain auth differences. Our CJS build still includes the old node-fetch retry shim; ESM build uses the new fetch-based retry hook. Mixing them means behavior differs in production.
thomas: Quick fix: switch to conditional exports so importers get the right entry: for example - "exports": { ".": { "import": "./dist/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/index.cjs.js" }, "./package.json": "./package.json" }
lia: And update the d.ts to use explicit ESM-style exports (default + named) instead of `export =`. That makes types resolve in bundlers/TS configs that expect ESM.
maria: I opened a PR with the changes (conditional exports, typing fix, changelog) and a patch candidate published to `next`: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1234 and npm: 0.11.2-rc.1
jamal: Can we add CI smoke tests? A tiny sample-app that runs rollup/esbuild + miniflare to ensure ESM import works on workers would catch regressions.
thomas: Good idea. Also keep `main` pointing to CJS for older tooling that ignores exports and looks only at main, and keep `module` pointing to the ESM bundle. Conditional exports + main/module covers most cases.
lia: Small follow-ups: update sample-apps docs to show edge import patterns and add a troubleshooting note: if your runtime pulls the wrong file try importing the explicit ESM bundle path: `import Redwood from 'redwood-inference/dist/index.mjs'`.
maria: Also adding a runtime guard: detect if `globalThis.fetch` exists and fallback to a no-op retry adapter instead of throwing when polyfills are missing. That should reduce silent auth failures.
publish-bot: build 0.11.2-rc.1 published to npm under `next`.
maria: Action items: @jamal add CI smoke test + sample-app repro, @lia land typing fixes, @thomas coordinate patch publish to `latest` and notify affected customers. I'll update onboarding checklist to include edge bundler import test.
jamal: putting a minimal repro in sample-apps repo and wiring the workflow today.
lia: pushed the typing tweak to the PR, changed `export =` -> `declare const Redwood: ...; export default Redwood; export { helper1, helper2 };`.
maria: Perfect. After we merge and ship patch we'll reach out to the reporting customer with the `next` rc for quick validation. :thumbsup:
